gate_rendering.evidenced_by: DISCOVER-9, built on DISCOVER-1 and DISCOVER-2
gate_rendering.line: Problem statement one sentence, stated the same way
Five or more real conversations or equivalent primary data, cited by source
Personas under five cited interviews marked as assumptions
Cost of inaction written down, calculation shown
A plausible no-go seriously argued
Domain selected from the domain index, or "none" recorded
Gate 6 success signal named now

gate_rendering.evidenced_by: The signed gate attempt itself; the Conductor never records this line as pass on its own authority
gate_rendering.line: Go or no-go recorded with rationale

questions.accept_when: one title, one company, one consequence, one citation.
questions.ask: Who exactly has this problem?
questions.cross_examine: the answer is a segment, a market, or a persona label. Move: category to name, one title, one named or precisely described company, one consequence that person personally eats.
questions.evidence: 4, interview claim, or better; a named user beats a cited quote.
questions.lands_in: `discovery/problem-framing.md` section 6 and `discovery/personas.md` evidence block, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: Every later stage is built for a composite nobody, and the beta is where you find out.

questions.accept_when: a dated action with a place it is recorded, or the workaround artifact named.
questions.ask: What did that person do the last time the problem occurred?
questions.cross_examine: the answer describes what they want, plan, or would do. Move: interest to behavior, what did someone pay, or what broke that caused a call?
questions.evidence: 1 or 2, observed behavior or an artifact of the workaround: a ticket, a spreadsheet, an export.
questions.lands_in: `discovery/problem-framing.md` section 4 and `discovery/journey-map.md`, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: Intentions poll well and predict nothing; you scope against behavior or against air.

questions.accept_when: number, unit, period, source, or a register row owning the guess.
questions.ask: What does the current workaround cost them, per what period?
questions.cross_examine: the number arrives without a unit, a period, and a source. Move: naked numbers, route to the assumptions register unless all three arrive.
questions.evidence: 2, artifact, or an explicit assumptions-register entry.
questions.lands_in: `discovery/problem-framing.md` section 5, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: A problem with no priced pain loses every roadmap argument it enters.

questions.accept_when: what it costs, whom, per what period, with the arithmetic visible.
questions.ask: What does it cost to do nothing?
questions.cross_examine: the answer is a fear, not a figure. Move: naked numbers.
questions.evidence: 2, artifact, or an explicit assumptions-register entry; the calculation shown either way.
questions.lands_in: `discovery/problem-framing.md` section 5 and `discovery/discovery-document.md` section 3, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: Without this line the honest default is to do nothing, and the gate should say so.

questions.accept_when: a count, with each source cited, where primary data counts only when it is first-hand and cited by source; below five, every persona is marked as an assumption before this answer is accepted.
questions.ask: How many real user conversations, or equivalent primary data (observed usage, support tickets, recorded sessions), stand behind this, and where are they cited?
questions.cross_examine: the count includes teammates, secondhand summaries, or "lots". Move: banned openers, then re-ask at class.
questions.evidence: 4, interview claims cited by source.
questions.lands_in: `discovery/discovery-document.md` section 2 citations and `discovery/personas.md` evidence blocks, and STATE.md accepted answers and evidence ledger.
questions.wrong_costs: Gate 1 requires five or more; fewer, undisclosed, turns personas into fiction the whole system then trusts.

questions.accept_when: one observable condition that, if seen, ends the initiative.
questions.ask: What would make the honest answer no-go?
questions.cross_examine: the answer is "nothing realistic" or restates the pitch. Move: banned openers, then ask what observation this month would kill it.
questions.evidence: 5, filed openly: a stated disconfirming condition someone could observe, because the condition, not its truth, is the deliverable.
questions.lands_in: `discovery/discovery-document.md` section 7, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: A gate that cannot fail is a ceremony, and Gate 1 requires the no-go case seriously argued.

questions.accept_when: signal, threshold or direction, source system, all named before any solution exists.
questions.ask: What observable signal, measurable at Gate 6, says this worked?
questions.cross_examine: the signal is an adjective or has no source system. Move: naked numbers.
questions.evidence: 2, a measurable signal plus the source system that will measure it.
questions.lands_in: `discovery/discovery-document.md` section 5, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: Named after launch, the signal becomes whatever the launch produced.

questions.accept_when: one card from the domain index named, or "none", either way recorded.
questions.ask: Which domain pack governs this product?
questions.cross_examine: a domain is claimed but no gatekeeper from its card can be named. Move: open the card together; if none of its rows bite, the honest answer is "none".
questions.evidence: 2, artifact: the chosen card's gatekeeper list in [../../../knowledge/domains/README.md](../../../knowledge/domains/README.md) consulted, or "none" recorded with the table checked.
questions.lands_in: STATE.md position block, `Domain:` line.
questions.wrong_costs: Every later gatekeeper and metric question gets answered generically, and the market-specific blocker surfaces at launch instead of here.

questions.accept_when: one sentence in the section 3 form, each clause citing the accepted answer ID it comes from.
questions.ask: In one sentence, with no solution words, what is the problem?
questions.cross_examine: the sentence names a feature, a solution, or needs two sentences to say. Move: banned openers, then: state it as a person, a circumstance, and a consequence, nothing else.
questions.evidence: 2, the accepted answers it cites: every clause traces to an accepted DISCOVER-1, DISCOVER-2, or DISCOVER-3 answer; this entry composes them, it does not gather new evidence.
questions.lands_in: `discovery/problem-framing.md` section 3, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: With no accepted sentence in this exact form, every later reader states the problem differently, and DEFINE-4 traces objectives to a sentence nobody agreed on.

Every acceptance criterion can fail

Assumptions register complete per assumption

gate_rendering.evidenced_by: Human signature on the one-pager, PRD, or BRD sign-off block; the Conductor reports presence or absence, never supplies it

AI overlay: eval sets with thresholds, not prose
Regulated overlay: section 0 answered per market, lint green

questions.accept_when: exactly one option, with one line of reasoning.
questions.ask: What does being wrong here cost?
questions.cross_examine: the answer hedges across two options. Move: banned openers, then force one.
questions.evidence: 5 is acceptable, this is a judgment the user owns; the judgment must still pick one option.
questions.lands_in: `execution/decision-log.md` weight entry and STATE.md accepted answers, at every weight.
questions.options: a) an afternoon, which implies decide and log or a ticket. b) a sprint, which implies a ticket with acceptance criteria. c) a quarter, which implies a one-pager or a full PRD. d) a license or a contract, which implies the full stack and a regulatory look.
questions.wrong_costs: Weight follows stakes; misjudge this and either a quarter of work gets a ticket or a two-day change gets a twelve-section spec.

questions.accept_when: each reader named with the action their reading triggers.
questions.ask: Who must read this document and act on it?
questions.cross_examine: the answer is "the team" or "stakeholders". Move: category to name.
questions.evidence: 5, a judgment the user owns: named roles, or named people where they exist.
questions.lands_in: `execution/decision-log.md` weight entry always; at one-pager weight, also `definition/one-pager.md` "Reviewers who must not be surprised" once DEFINE-3 lands the weight (full-PRD and BRD-stack weight route this answer to section 3 "Users and stories" of the PRD and section 4 "Stakeholders" of the BRD instead, filled during those templates' own drafting), and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: A document written for nobody in particular is read by nobody at all.

questions.accept_when: reversible with the mechanism named, or irreversible with what it locks in named. The three answers so far pick the weight; the Conductor states the pick and why before continuing.
questions.ask: Can this be undone in a day with a flag, or does it set contracts, data models, or public commitments that outlive the team?
questions.cross_examine: "we can always roll it back" arrives with no named mechanism. Move: interest to behavior, has that rollback ever been performed?
questions.evidence: 2 where the claim is a flag or a rollback path, an artifact should exist; otherwise a reasoned judgment.
questions.lands_in: `execution/decision-log.md` weight entry, plus `definition/one-pager.md` section 3 "Scope" at one-pager weight (full-PRD and BRD-stack weight route this answer into section 4 "Functional scope" of the PRD instead, filled during that template's own drafting), and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: Treating a one-way door as reversible is how a weekend decision becomes a two-year migration.

questions.accept_when: every objective traces, or the untraced ones are cut or explicitly flagged as new scope needing its own discovery.
questions.ask: Which Gate 1 problem statement does each objective trace to?
questions.cross_examine: an objective traces to a goal, a competitor, or a wish instead of the Gate 1 problem. Move: banned openers, then: cut it, or name the gap out loud in the document.
questions.evidence: 2, the trace itself, objective to problem statement, line by line.
questions.lands_in: `definition/prd.md` section 2 at full-PRD or BRD-stack weight; `definition/one-pager.md` section 4 at one-pager weight, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: An objective that traces to nothing is scope smuggled past discovery.

questions.accept_when: every requirement has a failing condition a tester could stage. Prose that cannot fail is returned, not accepted.
questions.ask: For each requirement, how does it fail?
questions.cross_examine: a criterion contains "works well", "fast", "intuitive", or any word a demo could not falsify. Move: naked numbers, threshold or it is not a criterion.
questions.evidence: 2, a condition, an expected result, and a measurable threshold per requirement.
questions.lands_in: `definition/acceptance-criteria.md`, plus `definition/frd.md` at BRD-stack weight, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: Prose that cannot fail cannot be tested, and its gaps ship silently.

questions.accept_when: the list is written and the sponsor's acknowledgment is dated.
questions.ask: What is out of scope, and has the sponsor read the list?
questions.cross_examine: the list exists but the sponsor has "seen it around". Move: interest to behavior, where is the written yes?
questions.evidence: 3, named commitment, the sponsor's written acknowledgment of the list.
questions.lands_in: `definition/prd.md` section 7 at full-PRD or BRD-stack weight; `definition/one-pager.md` section 5 at one-pager weight, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: The unwritten exclusion is the launch-week surprise, delivered by the sponsor.

questions.accept_when: each assumption carries all three fields and an owner.
questions.ask: Which assumptions is this built on?
questions.cross_examine: the register is empty or every confidence is high. Move: banned openers, an empty register on a new product is itself the strongest claim in the room.
questions.evidence: 5, filed properly: each assumption gets a confidence, a validation method, and a validate-by date.
questions.lands_in: `definition/assumptions-register.md` section 1, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: The unsigned assumption is the one that resurfaces in the launch review.

questions.accept_when: both halves answered with grounds. Yes to the model half attaches the AI overlay, eval rows replacing prose criteria via [../../ai-prd/SKILL.md](../../ai-prd/SKILL.md). Yes to the regulator half routes through [../../reg-gap-check/SKILL.md](../../reg-gap-check/SKILL.md) before Gate 2, because the regulated overlay's preconditions freeze here. Yes to both halves activates the regulated overlay itself, which is the rule in [../../../os/STAGE-GATES.md](../../../os/STAGE-GATES.md); a yes on the regulator half alone does not, and STATE.md records what the regulatory owner carries instead.
questions.ask: Does a model produce any user-facing output, and does a financial or data regulator govern any target market?
questions.cross_examine: either half is "probably not". Move: banned openers, then: which markets, which data, which model, checked against what?
questions.evidence: 5, a stated yes or no per half, each with one line of grounds.
questions.lands_in: STATE.md position block (overlays active) and `execution/decision-log.md`, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: A deferred overlay resurfaces later with an eval gap or a regulator's reference number attached.

questions.accept_when: a filled inventory, or a stated reason the product has no UI.
questions.ask: Does this change have a user-facing surface? If so, does the UI state inventory list every screen's states with an owner?
questions.cross_examine: the answer is "we have a UI" but the inventory is missing or incomplete. Move: banned openers, then: name every screen, name its states, name its owner.
questions.evidence: 2, the inventory, or a stated reason the product has no UI.
questions.lands_in: `definition/ui-state-inventory.md` and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: A screen whose states are unlisted ships with gaps in behavior, accessibility, and ownership.

gate_rendering.line: At least one rejected alternative recorded as an ADR
Every integration names owner, protocol, SLA, failure behavior
Data model classifies PII with retention per class

gate_rendering.evidenced_by: DESIGN-3, plus the architect-agent trust-boundary walk against `architecture/security-architecture.md`
gate_rendering.line: Security walk per component with mitigation owners
Observability names SLOs, thresholds, dashboard owner
A premortem ran and the risk register absorbed it
High risks have named owners and review dates
Dependency register complete with escalation contacts
AI overlay: least access, guardrails owned and tested

questions.accept_when: a real alternative, the tradeoff that decided against it, and the consequence accepted by deciding.
questions.ask: What alternative was seriously considered and rejected, and what tradeoff decided it?
questions.cross_examine: the alternative is a strawman nobody would have built. Move: banned openers, then: what would a competent team choosing it have been optimizing for?
questions.evidence: 2, the tradeoff written as an ADR.
questions.lands_in: `architecture/adr.md` (one ADR per decision, suffix names the decision), and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: A design with no rejected alternative has not been designed yet; it has been transcribed.

questions.accept_when: every integration row carries owner, SLA, and failure behavior, and no row says it will be worked out later.
questions.ask: For every integration, who owns it, under what SLA, and what happens when it fails?
questions.cross_examine: the failure behavior is retry-and-hope, or the owner is a team, not a person. Move: category to name.
questions.evidence: 3, the counterparty's commitment in writing, or the gap named per integration.
questions.lands_in: `architecture/integrations.md` sections 1 and 3, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: "We will figure it out" at design time becomes an incident owned by whoever is on call.

questions.accept_when: every data class marked, retention stated per class, and the deletion path named.
questions.ask: Where does personally identifiable information live, and what is the retention per data class?
questions.cross_examine: "we do not really store PII" arrives without a walked data model. Move: interest to behavior, walk the model field by field.
questions.evidence: 2, the data model with classes marked and retention stated.
questions.lands_in: `architecture/data-model.md` and `architecture/security-architecture.md`, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: Retention decided after launch is retention decided by whoever gets the deletion request.

questions.accept_when: two distinct failure causes, each landed in the risk register with a likelihood, an impact, a named owner and a review date in the future; any score of 6 or more carries an active mitigation with a trigger, per the register's exit gate. Then hand off to [../../program-premortem/SKILL.md](../../program-premortem/SKILL.md) for the full twelve-mode pass; its PRESENT findings join the same register.
questions.ask: It is six months from now and this product failed: why?
questions.cross_examine: the first answer is generic (ran late, lost focus) or the second answer repeats the first. Move: banned openers; this question is always asked twice, and the second answer must differ from the first.
questions.evidence: 5, filed as owned risks; the deliverable is the register row, not certainty.
questions.lands_in: `execution/risk-register.md` section 2, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: Teams reliably know how their project will fail and reliably are not asked.

questions.accept_when: every dependency has a needed-by date, an escalation contact, and evidence of the counterparty's commitment or an honest register row saying it is unconfirmed.
questions.ask: Which teams does this product wait on, by what date, and who is the escalation contact?
questions.cross_examine: "they know about it". Move: interest to behavior, is it in their plan with a date, and can you point at it?
questions.evidence: 3, the dependency in the other team's committed plan, not only in yours.
questions.lands_in: `execution/dependency-register.md` sections 1 and 2, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: The dependency discovered at integration time is owned by a team that never agreed to your date.

questions.accept_when: SLOs with numbers, alert thresholds, and one named dashboard owner.
questions.ask: How will you see this misbehaving before users tell you?
questions.cross_examine: the answer is "standard monitoring" or a tool name with no thresholds. Move: naked numbers.
questions.evidence: 2, SLOs, alert thresholds, and a dashboard owner written down before code exists.
questions.lands_in: `architecture/observability.md` sections 1, 4, and 5, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: Without SLOs and alerts named now, the monitoring plan is the support queue.

questions.accept_when: every agent's access is the minimum its task needs, and every guardrail row names an owner and a test. Skip this entry with a cited source when STATE.md says the AI overlay is not active.
questions.ask: What is the least access each agent needs, and does every guardrail have an owner and a test?
questions.cross_examine: any agent holds access "for flexibility", or any guardrail's test is a design review. Move: interest to behavior, show the test that exercised it.
questions.evidence: 2, the permission table and the guardrail table, each row owned and tested.
questions.lands_in: `definition/ai/agent-architecture.md` permission table and `definition/ai/guardrails.md` guardrail table, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: An over-permissioned agent is a breach with a project plan; an untested guardrail is a diagram.

questions.accept_when: a record with section 6 decided, or a stated reason the product has no UI.
questions.ask: Does this change have a user-facing surface? If so, where is the design review record, and which accessibility checklist evidence cells are filled?
questions.cross_examine: the answer is "no UI" without a stated reason, or the record exists but section 6 is undecided. Move: interest to behavior, show the checklist cells.
questions.evidence: 2, the record.
questions.lands_in: `architecture/design-review-record.md` and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: A product with a UI ships without a walked design review or without accessibility evidence because no gate asked for either.

gate_rendering.line: Every criterion demonstrated passing, or a miss with owner and decision
No edge-case row undecided; expected behavior and linked test per case
Failure scenarios exercised, detection fired, recovery matched

gate_rendering.evidenced_by: BUILD-1, via the acceptance-agent evidence ledger against `delivery/testing-strategy.md`
gate_rendering.line: Coverage meets targets, gaps listed by name
Scope changes since Gate 2 all in the decision log with deciders
AI overlay: evals ran on the shipping version, red team clean or escalated

questions.accept_when: every Gate 2 criterion maps to a passing run, or appears as a miss with an owner and a decision.
questions.ask: Which acceptance criteria are demonstrated passing, and for each miss, who owns it and what was decided?
questions.cross_examine: the answer is a coverage figure or "the suite is green" with no mapping to criteria. Move: naked numbers, then: which criterion, which run, where recorded?
questions.evidence: 2, test results a reader could open, criterion by criterion.
questions.lands_in: `delivery/testing-strategy.md` results section, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: "Code complete" quietly replaces "criteria met", and the difference ships to customers.

questions.accept_when: the undecided count is zero; anything else is a named miss with an owner. Every case has an expected behavior and a linked test.
questions.ask: Which edge-case rows are still undecided?
questions.cross_examine: the register is suspiciously short for the surface area. Move: banned openers, then walk the hunting list in the template together.
questions.evidence: 2, the edge-case register itself.
questions.lands_in: `delivery/edge-cases.md` section 2, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: The rows nobody decided become production incidents decided by whoever is on call.

questions.accept_when: each scenario in the table was exercised, detection fired, recovery matched or the divergence is written up.
questions.ask: Were the failure scenarios exercised, and did detection fire and recovery match the write-up?
questions.cross_examine: "we tested failures" arrives without a date or a scenario name. Move: interest to behavior, which scenario, run when, observed where?
questions.evidence: 1, the exercise itself, dated, with what fired and what recovered.
questions.lands_in: `delivery/failure-scenarios.md` sections 1 and 3, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: A failure plan that was never run is a guess with a table of contents.

questions.accept_when: every change is logged with a decider, including the rejections.
questions.ask: What changed in scope since Gate 2, and where is each change in the decision log with a decider named?
questions.cross_examine: "nothing really changed" on a build of any length. Move: banned openers, then diff the shipped surface against the Gate 2 scope list together.
questions.evidence: 2, decision-log entries, one per change, each with a decider.
questions.lands_in: `execution/decision-log.md`, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: Scope absorbed to be agreeable leaves a baseline that no longer describes the product.

questions.accept_when: the run is against the shipping version and every threshold passed or its miss is escalated with an owner. Skip this entry with a cited source when STATE.md says the AI overlay is not active.
questions.ask: Did the eval sets run against the model version that ships, and what happened at each threshold?
questions.cross_examine: the run predates the current model version, or a threshold miss is explained rather than escalated. Move: naked numbers.
questions.evidence: 2, the eval run, version-stamped, threshold by threshold.
questions.handle: AI overlay, evals on the shipping version
questions.lands_in: `definition/ai/eval-spec.md` results section, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: An eval suite run against last month's model is the most common way a green spec produces a red launch.

questions.accept_when: findings listed, every fix re-tested, no unfixed break rated high.
questions.ask: What did the red team break, and was every fix re-tested?
questions.cross_examine: the red team found nothing, or a fix's re-test is "should be fine now". Move: banned openers; a clean red-team pass on a first attempt is a finding about the red team.
questions.evidence: 2, the red-team findings and the re-test evidence per fix.
questions.lands_in: `definition/ai/red-team-review.md` and `execution/risk-register.md` for accepted residual risk, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: A fix that was never re-attacked is a hypothesis wearing a checkmark.

gate_rendering.line: UAT exit criteria met, severity-1 defects closed
Rollback performed in pre-production, time recorded
Known issues listed with workaround or accepted-risk sign-off

gate_rendering.evidenced_by: DELIVER-11, with DELIVER-5 for the support row
gate_rendering.line: Comms drafted and approved
On-call informed, runbook exists

gate_rendering.evidenced_by: Human signatures; the Conductor reports presence or absence, never supplies them
gate_rendering.line: Every function signed its own readiness line

gate_rendering.evidenced_by: DELIVER-12, with BUILD-5 and BUILD-6 re-verified against the release candidate
gate_rendering.line: AI overlay: guardrails live, kill switch tested
Regulated overlay: section 0 still true of what ships

questions.accept_when: performed, dated, timed, in a pre-production environment.
questions.ask: Was the rollback actually performed in pre-production, and how long did it take?
questions.cross_examine: "we have a rollback plan" arrives as a document, not a rehearsal. Move: interest to behavior, when was it run and how long did it take?
questions.evidence: 1, the rehearsal, dated, with the time to roll back recorded.
questions.lands_in: `delivery/release-readiness.md` section 4, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: The industry's incident write-ups repeat one line: the rollback plan existed on paper and had never been run.

questions.accept_when: exit criteria met, testers real or named proxies, severity-1 count zero.
questions.ask: Are the UAT exit criteria met with real users or named proxies, and is every severity-1 defect closed?
questions.cross_examine: the testers are teammates standing in for users without being named as proxies. Move: category to name.
questions.evidence: 2, UAT results against the plan's exit criteria, testers named.
questions.lands_in: `delivery/uat-plan.md` section 6, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: UAT signed by the build team is the build team agreeing with itself.

questions.accept_when: every shipping issue listed with a workaround or a signed acceptance.
questions.ask: Which known issues ship, each with a workaround or an accepted-risk signature?
questions.cross_examine: the list is empty on a first release. Move: banned openers; zero known issues is a claim about your testing, not your product.
questions.evidence: 3, each accepted risk signed by someone with standing.
questions.lands_in: `delivery/release-readiness.md` section 3, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: The unlisted known issue becomes support's discovery and the team's credibility bill.

questions.accept_when: a named cohort, one channel, and prior evidence the channel reaches them.
questions.ask: Who is the first user cohort, through which channel, and what evidence says that channel reaches them?
questions.cross_examine: the cohort is a segment or the channel is "marketing". Move: category to name.
questions.evidence: 2, evidence the channel has reached these people before.
questions.lands_in: the workspace gtm plan, first cohort section, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: A launch aimed at everybody arrives for nobody; the beachhead is a choice you defend.

questions.accept_when: named acknowledgment from support and on-call, runbook path stated.
questions.ask: Do support and on-call know this release is coming, and does the runbook exist?
questions.cross_examine: "they have been looped in" without a named acknowledgment. Move: interest to behavior, who confirmed, and where is the runbook?
questions.evidence: 3, their acknowledgment, plus the runbook as an artifact.
questions.lands_in: `delivery/release-readiness.md` sections 5 and 6, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: The launch support learns about from customers is the other repeat offender in incident write-ups.

questions.accept_when: each answer re-verified, and any drift written up and re-signed by the regulatory owner. Where STATE.md records that the shipped overlay did not apply and names what the regulatory owner used in its place, the Gate 5 line re-checks that substitute instead, by name, in the same way. Skip this entry with a cited source only when STATE.md records that no regulator applies to the product.
questions.ask: Are the section 0 answers from Gate 2 still true of the artifact that ships?
questions.cross_examine: "nothing changed" without the line-by-line check. Move: interest to behavior, walk the four together.
questions.evidence: 2, the answers re-checked line by line against the shipping artifact: model version, vendor terms, data residency, disclosures.
questions.lands_in: `delivery/release-readiness.md` section 7, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: A deferred precondition can resurface with a regulator's reference number attached.

questions.accept_when: one named alternative, one sentence a real cohort member would repeat.
questions.ask: Against which named alternative is this positioned, and what is the one sentence the first cohort hears?
questions.cross_examine: the alternative is "doing nothing" claimed without DISCOVER-2 behavior behind it, or the sentence needs three clauses. Move: banned openers.
questions.evidence: 4, the alternative named from discovery evidence, not assumed.
questions.lands_in: the workspace gtm plan, positioning section, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: Positioned against nothing, the product is compared to everything, on the buyer's terms.

questions.accept_when: ordered steps, each owned and dated, with the first reversible step first.
questions.ask: In what order do the launch steps run, and who owns each step?
questions.cross_examine: steps have owners but no dates, or the sequence is a single big-bang day. Move: naked numbers.
questions.evidence: 2, the sequence written with owners and dates.
questions.lands_in: the workspace gtm plan, launch sequence section, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: A launch without a sequence is a date with hope attached.

questions.accept_when: one metric, one threshold or direction, one date, one source system.
questions.ask: What is the one metric that says the launch worked, and by when?
questions.cross_examine: multiple metrics arrive, or the metric contradicts DISCOVER-7 without explanation. Move: naked numbers.
questions.evidence: 2, a measurable signal plus the source system that will measure it, consistent with the Gate 1 signal from DISCOVER-7.
questions.lands_in: the workspace gtm plan, success measure section, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: Without one metric named in advance, the retrospective grades on a curve of whatever moved.

questions.accept_when: condition, threshold, and the person with authority to pull it, named.
questions.ask: What condition pauses the rollout?
questions.cross_examine: the condition is "if things look bad". Move: naked numbers.
questions.evidence: 3, the named authority's commitment to call the stop: an observable condition with a threshold and that authority named.
questions.lands_in: the workspace gtm plan, stop condition section, and `execution/risk-register.md`, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: A rollout with no stop condition stops only when the damage does.

questions.accept_when: every row of release-readiness section 6 has an owner, an approver named from evidence, and a sent or scheduled date.
questions.ask: For each audience (support, sales or field, customers), is the message drafted, and who approved it in writing?
questions.cross_examine: an audience row has a message and no approver, or "we'll send something" stands in for a draft. Move: interest to behavior, who approved it and when?
questions.evidence: 3, named commitment per audience, or "silent release" recorded with its decider.
questions.lands_in: `delivery/release-readiness.md` section 6, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: A drafted message with no named approver ships as whatever the last editor left in it, and nobody is accountable for the version that went out.

questions.accept_when: guardrail rows re-verified against the release candidate, and the kill switch pulled, dated, timed, runner named. Skip this entry with a cited source when STATE.md says the AI overlay is not active.
questions.ask: Were the guardrails verified live in the release candidate, and when was the kill switch last pulled there, by whom, and how long until fully stopped?
questions.cross_examine: the switch is described, not pulled, or one flag takes the host surface down too. Move: interest to behavior.
questions.evidence: 1, the rehearsal in the release candidate, dated and timed.
questions.lands_in: the workspace copy of `templates/ai/guardrails.md` section 4 (Last tested) and `delivery/release-readiness.md` section 5, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: A kill switch that was designed but never tested is a fail dressed as a pass; the first real pull is the worst possible time to discover it does not work.

gate_rendering.line: Gate 1 signal measured, source and calculation stated
Every key result scored number versus number
Input metrics examined, not just the headline
Operational load reviewed
Decision is one of persist, pivot, sunset
The decision's consequence is scheduled

gate_rendering.evidenced_by: Drafted by the Conductor from the accepted answers, confirmed word by word by the user before filing
gate_rendering.line: What this pass taught us, three sentences, filed findably
AI overlay: production evals compared with Gate 5, new populations re-evaluated

questions.accept_when: the same signal, measured, with source system and calculation a reader could re-run.
questions.ask: Was the Gate 1 success signal measured, with the source system and the calculation stated?
questions.cross_examine: the signal reported differs from the one DISCOVER-7 accepted, or the calculation is not shown. Move: naked numbers.
questions.evidence: 2, the measurement, source system and calculation shown.
questions.lands_in: `operate/metrics-review.md` section 1, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: A signal promised at DISCOVER and unmeasured at OPERATE means the loop never closed and nobody can say whether the product worked.

questions.accept_when: every key result scored actual against target, misses included.
questions.ask: For each key result, what is the number against the number?
questions.cross_examine: any result arrives as "strong", "on track", or "improving". Move: naked numbers.
questions.evidence: 2, actual versus target per key result. Adjectives are returned unanswered.
questions.lands_in: `operate/metrics-review.md` section 1, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: Adjectives grade themselves; a target either was hit or was not.

questions.accept_when: each input metric's movement is stated and the headline's movement is attributed or honestly marked unexplained.
questions.ask: Did the input metrics move, or did the headline move for an unrelated reason?
questions.cross_examine: the headline moved and no input did, and the answer waves at momentum. Move: banned openers, then: what else changed in the period?
questions.evidence: 2, input metric movement examined alongside the headline.
questions.lands_in: `operate/metrics-review.md` section 2, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: A headline lifted by seasonality or a pricing change credits the product for weather.

questions.accept_when: incident count, support volume, and on-call load stated with sources for the review window.
questions.ask: What does this cost to run, in incidents, support volume, and on-call load?
questions.cross_examine: "operationally it is fine" without counts. Move: naked numbers.
questions.evidence: 2, the operational numbers from their source systems.
questions.lands_in: `operate/metrics-review.md` section 3 and `operate/operational-readiness-review.md`, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: A product that hits its targets while burning its operators is a resignation letter on a delay.

questions.accept_when: one input metric, one experiment, its cost, and what result would justify scaling it.
questions.ask: Which input metric is the next growth bet, and what is the cheapest experiment that would move it?
questions.cross_examine: the bet is on the headline itself, or the experiment starts at a quarter of work. Move: naked numbers, then: what is the version that costs a week?
questions.evidence: 2, the chosen input metric from OPERATE-3's examined set, plus an experiment with a cost attached.
questions.lands_in: the workspace growth plan, next bet section, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: Growth effort not aimed at an input metric is aimed at the headline, which no team can move directly.

questions.accept_when: one decision, one scheduled consequence with a date and an owner. The Conductor recommends, the humans at Gate 6 decide.
questions.ask: Is the decision persist, pivot, or sunset, and what consequence is scheduled?
questions.cross_examine: the answer is "keep watching it". Move: banned openers; watching is persisting without admitting the cost.
questions.evidence: 3, the decision of the humans at Gate 6: one of exactly three decisions, with its consequence scheduled: the next DISCOVER pass, the pivot's Gate 1, or the sunset plan with dates and an owner.
questions.lands_in: `operate/metrics-review.md` section 5 and `execution/decision-log.md`, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.options: a) persist, which implies the next DISCOVER pass is scheduled. b) pivot, which implies a new Gate 1 with a date. c) sunset, which implies a plan with dates and an owner.
questions.wrong_costs: The zombie portfolio is made of products where nobody decided anything.

questions.accept_when: the loop or channel named, with one observed completion.
questions.ask: What loop or channel actually drives the input metric you are betting on?
questions.cross_examine: the mechanism is "word of mouth" or "virality" unobserved. Move: interest to behavior, show one instance of the loop completing.
questions.evidence: 2, the mechanism traced: who does what, which triggers the metric, observed at least once.
questions.lands_in: the workspace growth plan, mechanism section, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: An experiment on a metric with no mechanism behind it is a lottery ticket with a dashboard.

questions.accept_when: one counter-metric, one threshold, watched over the same window.
questions.ask: Which counter-metric catches the damage if this experiment works for the wrong reason?
questions.cross_examine: "there is no downside". Move: banned openers; an experiment with no conceivable damage is not changing anything.
questions.evidence: 2, a measurable counter-metric with a threshold and the same review window as the experiment.
questions.lands_in: the workspace growth plan, guardrail section, and `operate/metrics-review.md` section 3, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: Growth that cannibalizes trust reports as success right up until the churn arrives.

questions.accept_when: a result threshold and a date, and the owner who calls it.
questions.ask: What result kills the experiment?
questions.cross_examine: the condition is "if it clearly fails". Move: naked numbers.
questions.evidence: 3, the owner's commitment to call it: an observable result plus a date, either of which ends it.
questions.lands_in: the workspace growth plan, kill condition section, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: Experiments without kill conditions become programs, and programs without results become furniture.

questions.accept_when: a per-segment comparison against the Gate 5 run, and a re-evaluation date for each population added since. Skip this entry with a cited source when STATE.md says the AI overlay is not active.
questions.ask: Were production-sampled evals for the review window compared with the Gate 5 run, per segment, and was every population added since Gate 5 re-evaluated before it went live?
questions.cross_examine: the comparison is aggregate only, with no segment breakdown, or a population added since Gate 5 carries no re-evaluation date. Move: naked numbers.
questions.evidence: 2, the dated eval run.
questions.handle: AI overlay, production evals against Gate 5
questions.lands_in: `definition/ai/eval-spec.md` results, and STATE.md accepted answers.
questions.wrong_costs: A model that drifted since Gate 5 ships a different answer to a different segment, and nobody would know until a customer does.
